questions.question: Describe how solids, liquids and gases behave, with one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A solid keeps its own shape and amount, like a brick. A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container but keeps the same amount, like water. A gas spreads out to fill any space, like air.

questions.question: Why is sugar a solid even though it can be poured?
questions.expected_answer: Sugar is made of many tiny grains, and each grain is a solid with its own shape. A pile of sugar makes a heap instead of spreading flat like a liquid.

questions.question: How do we know that air is there if we cannot see it?
questions.expected_answer: We can feel it when the wind blows, we can see it blow up a balloon or a soccer ball, and we can see it move washing on a line. An empty bottle pushed under water lets out bubbles of air.
